ASSA Advocate for the Petitioner : MR D TALUKDAR, MS P SAIKIA,MS B GOSWAMI,MR P CHOUDHURY Advocate for the Respondent : PP, ASSAM,
 BEFORE  HONOURABLE MRS. JUSTICE SUSMITA PHUKAN KHAUND  ORDER Date : 13.09.2024

Heard learned counsel Mr. P. Choudhury for the petitioners 1. Gannon Dunkerley and Co. Ltd., 2. Sri Subroto Mukherjee, 3. Sri Manoj Kumar Singh, 4. Sri Parag C Mehta, 5. Mrs.
Pragati Raghavdas Mundhra, 6. Mr. Ashish Kr. Pal, who have filed this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 read with Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 with prayer for quashing the order dated 02.03.2024 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate 1st Class, Dibrugarh wherein cognizance of offences under Sections 406/420/506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 was taken against the petitioners and thereafter, issuing summonses against them in connection with C.R. Case No. 132 C/2023.
2. It is submitted that now the petitioners' have learnt that non-bailable warrants have also been issued against them.
3. Heard Ms. S. Jahan, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Assam for the Page No.# 4/5 respondent State.
Learned Additional Public Prosecutor has accepted notice on behalf of the respondent No. 1 and thus, no formal notice is required to be issued.
However, sufficient copies of the petition to be furnished during the course of the day.

4. Issue notice to respondent Nos. 2 and 3 by registered post with A/D as well as through usual process, returnable on 01.10.2024.
5.

Call for the scanned copies of the Trial Court Records of C.R. Case No. 132C/2023.
6.
It is submitted on behalf of the petitioners that the respondents deal in supply of construction materials.

Work tender was issued in favour of the petitioners by the accused Nos. 1 to 5 mentioned in the complaint for construction of 4 lane highway from Jhanji to Demow and accordingly, the petitioners contacted the respondent firm for supplying of construction materials such as stone-chips, boulders, sand and gravel.

When the respondents enquired about the same, the petitioners deposited bank guarantee and accordingly, they received materials from the respondent No. 2 and from 31.08.2017 to 30.11.2019 and the value of the materials were Rs. 88.94 Lacs and accordingly, the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 have received payment for the materials except Rs.1,36,861/-.
Page No.# 1/5 vs The State Of Assam And 2 Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89076697/

3 7 . It is submitted on behalf of the petitioners that the petitioners could not pay the amount as the accused Nos. 1 to 5 named in the compliant did not release the funds and on 08.04.2022, the contract was terminated and another Company was awarded the contract.
8. It is submitted that no materials of cheating has been made out against Page No.# 5/5 the petitioners and this is a case of civil nature.
The petitioners' have paid more than 95 % of the valuation of the materials supplied to the Company.
9. I have considered the submissions at the bar with circumspection.

It appears that the petitioners have drawn out sufficient grounds for stay of the proceeding and thus, further proceedings of CR Case No. 132 C/2023 pending in the Court of JMFC, Dibrugarh is stayed till 01.10.2024.
10.
List accordingly.
